Science.title: GTA V flood simulations reveal how rising seas could reshape Los Santos
Science.summary: Grand Theft Auto V is one of the world's best-known video games. It is set in Los Santos, and although the city is fictional, its landscape and urban structure are modeled very closely on the American city of Los Angeles. Researchers from the Alfred Wegener Institute and the University of Potsdam have explored whether this virtual representation is detailed enough to realistically depict the consequences of a potential rise in sea levels and make them approachable.

Science.title: Study uncovers molecular mechanism underlying lip-related floral organ curvature in slipper orchids
Science.summary: A research team from the South China Botanical Garden (SCBG) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences has uncovered a molecular regulatory mechanism that contributes to the development of curved floral organs associated with the distinctive lips of orchids, offering new insights into the development and evolution of floral forms in orchids. The study was published in New Phytologist on Nov. 6.

Science.title: ESA’s Hera spacecraft is flying rectangles around NASA’s asteroid crash site
Science.summary: Europe’s Hera spacecraft has arrived at the scene of NASA’s historic asteroid collision to uncover what really happened when a spacecraft slammed into Dimorphos in 2022. Its close-up investigation could reveal whether the impact left a crater or reshaped the asteroid entirely, providing crucial clues for protecting Earth from future threats.

Science.title: At base of ocean food chain, scientists uncover impacts of a changing atmosphere
Science.summary: Much of the concern about elevated levels of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere focuses on its effects on global warming as a greenhouse gas. But up to 30% of emitted carbon dioxide is absorbed by the oceans, where it reacts with water to lower pH and leads to ocean acidification, which has enormous effects on the chemistry and biology of marine ecosystems.

Science.title: The Leonid meteor shower peaks tonight: How to see more than a dozen 'shooting stars' per hour
Science.summary: Up to 15 shooting stars per hour may be visible as the Leonids peak under dark skies tonight (Nov. 16 - 17), with the moon setting before the best viewing hours.

Science.title: Engineered gel controls particle release to help injured spinal cord cells recover in lab
Science.summary: Researchers at the FAMU-FSU College of Engineering have developed a gel that delivers therapeutic particles to injured spinal cord cells, a potential step toward new treatments for spinal cord injuries.

Science.title: Lasers near physical limits of miniaturization open possibilities for tracking life at the nanoscale
Science.summary: From tracking how cancer develops to exploring how the brain works, scientists need ways to observe biological processes at increasingly smaller scales. Beyond tracking how cells move and interact, researchers need to understand how tiny structures within cells, including organelles and molecular complexes, behave and change over time. However, identifying and tracking these microscopic targets individually remains a major challenge.

Science.title: Lava flows studied for their carbon dioxide storage potential
Science.summary: As global warming intensifies, scientists are exploring ways to reduce carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions. One emerging approach being explored in environmental research is carbon capture and storage (CCS), which involves capturing CO₂ and storing it deep underground, away from the atmosphere. In this context, researchers at the Indian Institute of Technology Gandhinagar (IITGN) have investigated ancient volcanic rocks in Maharashtra to assess their suitability for this purpose.

Science.summary: Physicists at the Large Hadron Collider have detected a rare, 1-in-10-billion particle interaction that opens a view into the 'zeptoverse,' the smallest distance scale ever measured.

Science.title: New Asian flying frog species identified in Indonesia
Science.summary: In the lush mountain rainforests of Indonesia, researchers have identified a new species of Asian flying frog with distinctive physical features, calls and unusual egg-laying habits. The discovery is described in a paper published in the journal Zootaxa by scientists from Museum Zoologicum Bogoriense in Indonesia, the University of California, Davis, and other collaborators.

Science.summary: Gravitational waves have revealed a population of black holes that may have been born when masssive stars failed to go supernova.

Science.title: Newly identified cell wall mechanism may help staph resist a last-resort antibiotic
Science.summary: Antimicrobial resistance represents one of the major challenges facing modern medicine. Especially worrying are bacteria that develop resistance to antibiotics that are the last available treatment options.

Science.title: The hidden language of psychopathy is not what scientists expected
Science.summary: Scientists have discovered that psychopathic traits are associated with surprisingly different patterns of language, with some individuals using more positive words and others expressing greater negativity or less anxiety. The findings challenge familiar stereotypes about psychopathy and suggest that the stories people tell about their lives may offer important clues about their personalities.

Science.title: Quantum-gas microscope resolves the 'color' of individual atoms in a single shot
Science.summary: In 2024, researchers at the Ultracold Quantum Gases group at ICFO built a quantum-gas microscope capable of imaging individual atoms in strontium quantum gases for the first time, marking a key enabling step for quantum simulation. At that time, the researchers imaged strontium-84, a boson that has no spin.

Science.title: Two proteins key to cellulose synthase trafficking and cell wall formation identified
Science.summary: A new study has identified Arabidopsis SNARE proteins VAMP726 and VAMP725 as key components of the trafficking of cellulose synthase (CESA), helping support the formation of both primary and secondary cell walls.

Science.title: Scientists tracked kids for 8 years. What they found about screen time was surprising
Science.summary: A surprising Finnish study found that children who spent more time using screens tended to have better cognitive processing abilities as teenagers, challenging the assumption that screen time is always harmful. Researchers suggest that what children do on screens may matter more than how much time they spend using them.

Science.summary: A Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL)-led team has harnessed the power of El Capitan to accelerate generation of predicted protein structures, drastically reducing the computing time required and opening new possibilities for drug discovery, biological research and national security applications.

Science.title: A material just one atom thick reveals a strange quantum secret
Science.summary: Researchers at the University of Osaka have discovered a remarkable quantum state forming at the boundary between a one-atom-thick material and a metal. They observed electrons behaving as though they were unusually heavy, including a previously unseen state created by interactions between the ultrathin layer and the copper beneath it. This first-of-its-kind observation reveals a promising new way to control exotic quantum behavior.

Science.title: Study tracks what students learn from online teamwork and fieldwork abroad
Science.summary: Can a solution that cuts food waste in Tokyo work in Seoul too? Exploring a familiar problem with peers abroad can help students question what they take for granted at home and see how their knowledge might apply to real-world sustainability challenges. As educators put time and care into designing international courses, what do students take away from the experience, and what stays with them after the course ends?

Science.title: Turning food waste into insect feed poses only low mad cow disease risk
Science.summary: Insects can convert food waste and by-products from the food industry (such as unsold ready meals or slaughter by-products) into ingredients for animal feed. In this way, they can contribute to the transition toward a circular food production system, in which what would otherwise be wasted is reused. However, these waste streams may contain animal proteins that pose a risk of transmitting diseases such as bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), also known as mad cow disease. For this reason, rearing insects on waste streams containing animal proteins is not permitted in the European Union.

Science.title: New model identifies priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile
Science.summary: Researchers from Chile's Institute of Ecology and Biodiversity (IEB) have developed a multiobjective model to identify priority areas for large-scale ecological restoration in Chile, South America. The tool integrates four ecological objectives: reducing species extinction risk, prioritizing carbon stocks, restoring riparian areas and assessing ecological feasibility. The findings show that including ecological feasibility changes restoration priorities, while 80.4% of the selected areas contribute to more than one ecological objective. Science.summary: Much of the news coverage on young men recently has focused on social media, gambling and the online "manosphere." But some of the most consequential changes in young men's lives are happening in school and workplaces.

Science.summary: A recent satellite photo captured an underwater cloud of fish sperm, or milt, appearing to glow green during a Pacific herring spawning event at a reproductive "sweet spot" along the coast of Canada's Vancouver Island.

Science.title: New platform improves accuracy of molecular counting in RNA-sequencing
Science.summary: The open-source platform, called UMIche (pronounced "you-me-kay"), is described in a new study published in Nature Communications. It addresses a common challenge in RNA-sequencing, where errors during sequencing can lead to inaccurate measurements of gene expression.

Science.title: How do human lifestyles affect the gut microbiome of our canine companions?
Science.summary: Dogs have been living side by side with humans for millennia, but a new study underscores how much we have yet to learn about man's best friend. The study, which looked at hundreds of dogs across four nations, found that the lifestyles of pet owners appear to play a significant role in determining what constitutes a healthy gut microbiome for their dog companions.
